trickyParts: The critical defect came from reading a frame's shape for a fact about the daemon. No agent_start of a live turn names a delivery — Oh My Pi never sets the field, the Claude Code bridge sends a bare start, and only the shim's replay of a start it already saw names one — so 'the start named no delivery' is true of every real turn and says nothing. What distinguishes the turn the daemon never saw is that nothing of the daemon's own was in flight to confirm it against: no send, no awaited turn, only askFirst. The tests hid it because they named a delivery id, which is the replay shape; every one of them now sends what a live shim sends.

ErrPodGone was chosen over a third result for the same reason the mask is applied only where it decides: a caller that does not know about the new answer must land on the safe side. An unnamed sentinel reads as an error, and groupDrift already treats an error as 'no statement that anything drifted, decide nothing'; an ignored boolean reads as 'present', which is the defect.

The notice and the replacement read the same claims but need different answers from them. The mask — a claim whose machine is deciding has not answered — is the replacement's caution before deleting a disk, not a property of the claim, so the notice is built unmasked: marked Answered: false, an answered claim is one the controller's playbook publishes to, and that publish takes the real answer back.

A role's own PostgreSQL is legion-testpg with LEGION_TESTPG_DIR under the issue's volume and a port of the role's own; this round's was 5447. Its role is NOSUPERUSER, so internal/daemon's outbox tests, which drop their database with FORCE, fail intermittently until `grant pg_signal_backend to legion_test` is run as the bootstrap superuser over the cluster's own socket under <LEGION_TESTPG_DIR>/sockets.
